create-cohort.title: How do I create a cohort?
create-cohort.description: Learn that the cohort is the annual container (one per year) for sections and courses, then walk through creation to the detail page.

create-section.title: How do I create a section?
create-section.description: After the year’s cohort exists, learn how to add a class group with teacher, dates, and weekly schedule — then land on the section detail page.

create-student.title: How do I create a student?
create-student.description: Learn the create-user form for students: how birth date decides whether a tutor is required, then walk the form without saving until you are ready.

create-teacher.title: How do I create a teacher?
create-teacher.description: Walk the create-user form with the teacher role: name, login email, password, and what happens when you submit later.

create-admin.title: How do I create an admin?
create-admin.description: Walk the create-user form with the admin role: staff access, credentials, and submitting only after the guided tour ends.

take-attendance.title: How do I take attendance?
take-attendance.description: Learn where section attendance lives, how the day/matrix views work, and how to mark presence without losing the weekly schedule context.

approve-payment.title: How do I approve a payment?
approve-payment.description: Walk the finance inbox: find pending receipts, understand tabs and bulk tools, and see where approve lives — without confirming a real approval.

reject-payment.title: How do I reject a payment?
reject-payment.description: Walk the finance inbox for a rejection path: locate the receipt, open reject, and learn why you must leave a clear reason — without confirming.

assign-scholarship-percent.title: How do I assign a partial scholarship?
assign-scholarship-percent.description: Open a student’s billing scholarship panel and learn how percent discounts apply to monthly fees — guide only; do not save until you are ready.

assign-scholarship-full.title: How do I assign a full scholarship?
assign-scholarship-full.description: Learn how a 100% scholarship covers tuition for a student from the billing panel — guide only; confirm yourself after the tour ends.

create-event.title: How do I create an event?
create-event.description: Learn the public events form: title, date, and pricing — then finish filling and submit yourself when you are ready to publish.

enable-mercadopago.title: How do I enable Mercado Pago?
enable-mercadopago.description: Open Finance settings and learn where Chile/Argentina Mercado Pago credentials live — guide only; never paste secrets during the tour.

enable-flow.title: How do I enable Flow Chile?
enable-flow.description: Walk Finance settings for Flow Chile credentials and save — guide only; do not submit real API keys during the tour.

change-billing-currency.title: How do I change billing currency?
change-billing-currency.description: Learn where institute billing currency is set and why changing it affects all fees — guide only; save yourself after the tour.

approve-event-payment.title: How do I approve an event payment?
approve-event-payment.description: Open an event’s Payments tab, review pending receipts, and learn where approve lives — guide only; never confirm a real approval during the tour.

assign-section-scholarship-bulk.title: How do I assign bulk scholarships in a section?
assign-section-scholarship-bulk.description: Walk Finance → Collections for a section: scholarships tab, bulk discount trigger, and modal fields — guide only; never confirm bulk apply during the tour.

change-site-setup-currency.title: How do I set billing currency in Initial setup?
change-site-setup-currency.description: Learn the Initial setup wizard Legal & billing step where institute currency is chosen — different from Finance settings; guide only; finish the wizard yourself after the tour.

create-blog-article.title: How do I create a blog article?
create-blog-article.description: Open the CMS blog editor: title, body, meta, and save — without publishing until you decide after the tour.

create-blog-article-as-teacher.title: How do I submit a blog article for review (teacher)?
create-blog-article-as-teacher.description: Same blog editor with emphasis on pending_review status for teacher-authored drafts — guide only; submit for review yourself after the tour.

reset-user-password.title: How do I reset a user password?
reset-user-password.description: Open a user profile Security tab and learn password reset controls — guide only; do not apply a password during the tour.

import-users.title: How do I import users from a spreadsheet?
import-users.description: Learn the Users → Import screen: choose a file and dry-run preview — the tour never starts a real import job.

existingCohortPrompt.title: Cohort {{year}} already exists
existingCohortPrompt.description: There is only one cohort per school year. We found «{{name}}» for {{year}}.
existingCohortPrompt.body: Do you want to continue with this cohort, or are you sure you want to create a new one for the same year?

handoffToCreateSection.title: 📂 Cohort is ready
handoffToCreateSection.description:
You are on the current cohort page. From here you can add sections —groups with schedule, teacher, and enrollments— and, within each section, the courses in your learning plan.

The natural next step is to create your first section inside this cohort.

intro.title: 🎯 Before you create sections or courses
intro.description:
A cohort is the top-level container in your academic structure: it represents the school year (for example “Cohort 2026”). There is only one cohort per year — you do not create separate morning or afternoon cohorts; those schedules belong in sections inside the cohort.

Inside each cohort live sections —classes with a schedule, teacher, and enrollments— and within each section, the courses or units in the learning plan.

You cannot create standalone sections or courses without a cohort. This tour walks you through that first step: define the annual container before you fill it.

navAcademic.title: 📚 Cohorts & sections
navAcademic.description:
Cohorts & sections is your academic control center: cohorts, sections, and enrollments in one place.

Click Next to open it. If you were on another admin screen, the tour navigates you to the hub automatically.

newCohort.title: ➕ New cohort
newCohort.description:
This button opens the form to create the cohort for the year. Without that annual container there is nowhere to attach the sections you will offer families later.

If the current year’s cohort already exists, use it instead of creating another. Click Next and the tour will open the modal for you.

nameField.title: ✏️ Cohort name
nameField.description:
Use the school year as the main reference. Example: “Cohort 2026” or “2026”. You do not need to split by shift — morning and afternoon are set when you create sections inside this cohort.

The slug is optional; leave it blank and the system generates one. The name must be at least 2 characters.

submit.title: ✅ Create cohort
submit.description:
When the name is clear and valid, confirm creation. The cohort is saved as an empty container — you will add sections from its detail page next.

The tour continues there to show you what comes after.

detail.title: 📂 Your cohort (container)
detail.description:
Done! You are on the page for the cohort you just created. This is the year’s container where sections live (with their morning, afternoon, or other schedules) and, inside each section, courses.

From here you can add sections, review enrollments, and run the cycle. Remember: one cohort per year — cohort first, then sections and courses inside it.

missingCohortNotice.title: Create a cohort first
missingCohortNotice.description:
Sections live inside a cohort (the annual container). We could not find a current or active-year cohort.

Run the “create a cohort” tutorial or open Cohorts & sections and create the year’s cohort before adding sections.

intro.title: 📋 Sections live inside the cohort
intro.description:
A section is the concrete class group families enroll in: name, teacher, school-year dates, weekly schedule (morning, afternoon, etc.), and capacity.

Unlike the cohort —one per year— you can have many sections in the same cohort. This tour assumes the year’s cohort already exists and walks you through adding your first or next section.

You will create a real section and end on its detail page.

sectionsTab.title: 📂 Sections tab
sectionsTab.description:
Inside each cohort, the Sections tab lists every class group for that year and the button to add a new one.

Click Next to focus this tab if it is not already selected.

newSection.title: ➕ New section
newSection.description:
Opens the form to define the class: teacher, dates, schedule slots, and optional capacity tweaks.

Click Next and the tour opens the modal for you.

basicsField.title: ✏️ Name and teacher
basicsField.description:
Give the section a clear name families will recognize (for example “Intermediate A — mornings”). Assign the lead teacher — required before saving.

If no teachers appear, add teacher profiles in Users first.

periodField.title: 📅 Section period
periodField.description:
Set when this section runs within the school year. Defaults usually match the institute calendar; adjust only if this group starts or ends on different dates.

Students outside this window should not remain enrolled without a deliberate change.

scheduleField.title: 🕐 Weekly schedule
scheduleField.description:
Add at least one weekly slot: weekday, start time, and end time. That is how morning vs afternoon (or Saturday) groups are distinguished — not by creating another cohort.

Use “add slot” for multiple meetings per week. Invalid or overlapping rows block creation.

submit.title: ✅ Create section
submit.description:
When name, teacher, dates, and schedule are valid, confirm creation. The section is saved under this cohort and you are taken to its detail page.

The tour finishes there with what you can do next.

detail.title: 🎓 Your new section
detail.description:
You are on the section detail page: roster, attendance, learning route, fees, and staff live here.

From the cohort’s Sections tab you can add more groups (other shifts or levels). Remember the order: cohort (year) → sections (classes) → courses inside each section.

birthDateBranch.title: 🎂 Minor or adult student?
birthDateBranch.description:
Birth date drives the rest of the form.

Choose a path below — the tour fills a sample birth date so you can see either the tutor/guardian block (minor) or the student email fields (adult). Nothing is saved until you click Create after the tour ends.

intro.title: 👤 Create a student (guide only)
intro.description:
This tour explains the Users → Add form for students. Nothing is saved until you click Create after the tour ends.

Key rule: for students, birth date decides if a tutor is required. Minors need a guardian (existing parent or a new tutor profile). Adults need their own email.

navUsers.title: 👥 Users
navUsers.description:
Open Users from the sidebar to manage profiles: students, teachers, admins, and more.

Click Next — if you were elsewhere, the tour opens the create form for you.

navAdd.title: ➕ Add user
navAdd.description:
Use Add (not Import CSV) when creating one person at a time. Import is for bulk CSV workflows.

You should now be on the create-user form.

role.title: 🎭 Role: Student
role.description:
Choose Student so the form shows birth date and, when needed, the tutor block. Other roles hide those student-only fields.

The tour selects Student for you when this step highlights.

nameFields.title: ✏️ Name
nameFields.description:
Enter surname and given name as they should appear on lists and documents. Use the same order your institute expects on official records.

You can fill these after the tour; this step only shows where they live.

dni.title: 🪪 Document ID
dni.description:
For minors, document ID is required so the profile can be linked and invited correctly. For adults it is optional but still useful for search and billing.

Do not invent a fake ID during a practice pass unless you intend to save.

birthDate.title: 🎂 Birth date
birthDate.description:
This control compares age to the institute’s majority setting. Under majority → tutor panel and synthetic login email hint. At or above majority → student email field, no tutor.

On the next step you choose which path to explore.

minorHint.title: ✉️ Minor login email
minorHint.description:
Minors usually get a system-generated login email; you do not type a personal inbox here. The guardian’s contact is what staff use for family communication.

Document ID remains required for this path.

guardianPanel.title: 👨‍👩‍👧 Tutor / guardian
guardianPanel.description:
Because this student is a minor, you must link a tutor before creating the profile. The panel appears only after birth date makes them under majority.

You can link an existing parent/guardian or create a new tutor in the same flow.

guardianMode.title: 🔗 Existing or new tutor
guardianMode.description:
Existing: search for a parent already in the system and pick them. New: fill tutor name, document, and optional email/phone to create and link them.

Switching modes clears the other side’s fields — choose deliberately.

guardianExistingVsNew.title: 🔎 Tutor details
guardianExistingVsNew.description:
If you chose existing, use the search box (prefix match on name or document). If you chose new, complete the tutor fields shown here.

Either way you still set the relationship on the next control.

relationship.title: 🤝 Relationship
relationship.description:
Say how the tutor relates to the student (mother, father, guardian, etc.). Required for a valid minor create.

Pick the code that matches your records — it appears on the student profile later.

adultEmail.title: ✉️ Student email
adultEmail.description:
Adult students sign in with their own email. Enter a real address you control if you will submit after the tour.

No tutor panel appears on this path.

phone.title: 📞 Phone (optional)
phone.description: Phone is optional for adult students. Add it when you have a reliable contact number for reminders and support.

password.title: 🔑 Password
password.description:
Optional initial password. If left blank, invite/reset flows can still grant access depending on institute settings.

Follow your password policy before a real create.

submitGuide.title: ✅ Create — after the tour
submitGuide.description:
This button saves the user for real. The tutorial stops here on purpose: finish filling fields, review tutor/email rules, then click Create yourself when ready.

Closing the tour does not discard what you typed in the form.

intro.title: 👩‍🏫 Create a teacher (guide only)
intro.description:
Teachers appear in section assignment and class tools. This tour walks the create-user form with role Teacher.

Nothing is saved until you click Create after the tour.

navUsers.title: 👥 Users
navUsers.description:
Teachers are created under Users → Add, same form as other roles — only the role field changes the outcome.

The tour opens the form if needed.

navAdd.title: ➕ Add user
navAdd.description: Use Add for a single teacher profile. Prefer Import only for bulk CSV onboarding.

role.title: 🎭 Role: Teacher
role.description:
Select Teacher. Birth date and tutor blocks stay hidden — those are student-only.

The tour sets Teacher when this step highlights.

nameFields.title: ✏️ Name
nameFields.description: Enter the teacher’s surname and given name as staff should see them in section pickers and messages.

email.title: ✉️ Login email
email.description: Teachers need a real email they can use to sign in. Use an address you control if you will create after the tour.

password.title: 🔑 Password
password.description: Optional initial password. Respect institute password rules before a real create.

submitGuide.title: ✅ Create — after the tour
submitGuide.description: Submit creates the teacher for real. Finish the form, then click Create yourself when ready. The tour does not save.

intro.title: 🛡️ Create an admin (guide only)
intro.description:
Admins can reach staff tools across the institute. Only create admin accounts for trusted people.

This tour guides the form; it does not submit.

navUsers.title: 👥 Users
navUsers.description:
Admin profiles are created from Users → Add with role Admin.

The tour navigates to the form if you started elsewhere.

navAdd.title: ➕ Add user
navAdd.description: Use Add for one admin at a time. Double-check role before you ever submit.

role.title: 🎭 Role: Admin
role.description:
Select Admin for full staff access. Prefer Teacher or other roles when admin privileges are not required.

The tour sets Admin on this step.

nameFields.title: ✏️ Name
nameFields.description: Use the person’s legal or preferred staff name so audit and messaging stay clear.

email.title: ✉️ Login email
email.description: Admins sign in with email. Prefer an institute-managed address when possible.

password.title: 🔑 Password
password.description: Optional initial password. Strong credentials matter more for admin accounts.

submitGuide.title: ✅ Create — after the tour
submitGuide.description: Submit creates the admin for real. Review role and email carefully, then click Create yourself when ready.

intro.title: 📅 Create an event (guide only)
intro.description:
Events appear on the public calendar and can carry optional ticket pricing.

This tour opens the create form and explains the main fields. Nothing is saved until you click Create after the tour ends.

createCta.title: ➕ New event
createCta.description:
From the events list, this control opens the create form.

If you already landed on /events/new, the tour skips straight to the form.

form.title: 📝 Event form
form.description:
Everything needed to publish lives here: identity, schedule, and optional pricing.

Keep titles clear for families browsing the public site.

titleField.title: ✏️ Title
titleField.description:
Use a short name families will recognize (workshop, recital, open house).

Avoid internal codes in the public title.

dateField.title: 📆 Date and time
dateField.description:
Set when the event happens. Wrong times confuse registrations and calendar sync.

Double-check timezone expectations for your institute.

pricing.title: 💳 Pricing (optional)
pricing.description:
Free events leave amounts empty. Paid events need clear prices before you publish.

Gateway setup is separate under Finance settings.

submitGuide.title: ✅ Create — after the tour
submitGuide.description:
Submit publishes the event for real. Finish the fields, review visibility, then click Create yourself when ready.

Closing the tour does not discard what you typed.

intro.title: ✅ Approve a payment (guide only)
intro.description:
Families upload receipts or pay online; staff confirm them in the finance inbox.

This tour shows where approval lives. It never clicks Confirm — approving is irreversible for billing state.

tabs.title: 📑 Finance tabs
tabs.description:
Inbox is where pending receipts wait. Other tabs cover history, settings, and reports.

Stay on Inbox for review work.

inbox.title: 📥 Payment inbox
inbox.description:
This workspace lists receipts waiting for a decision.

Filters and type chips narrow monthly tuition, enrollment, or invoices.

typeNav.title: 🏷️ Receipt types
typeNav.description:
Switch between monthly, enrollment, and invoice queues so you do not mix fee kinds.

Counts help you see what still needs attention.

bulkToolbar.title: 🧰 Bulk actions
bulkToolbar.description:
When several rows are selected, bulk tools appear for batch review.

Prefer single-row review until you trust the queue.

action.title: ✔️ Approve control
action.description:
Approve marks the receipt as accepted and updates billing.

The tour stops before Confirm — read amount and student carefully first.

empty.title: 📭 Empty inbox
empty.description:
If nothing is pending, this empty state is normal.

Come back when families upload new receipts.

intro.title: ❌ Reject a payment (guide only)
intro.description:
Reject when a receipt is illegible, duplicated, or does not match the amount due.

This tour highlights reject without confirming — always leave a clear reason for the family.

tabs.title: 📑 Finance tabs
tabs.description: Use Inbox for decisions. History shows past outcomes if you need context.

inbox.title: 📥 Payment inbox
inbox.description:
Find the receipt that should not be accepted.

Open the row to inspect the file before rejecting.

typeNav.title: 🏷️ Receipt types
typeNav.description:
Pick the correct fee queue so you reject the right billing kind.

Mixing types creates support confusion.

bulkToolbar.title: 🧰 Bulk actions
bulkToolbar.description: Bulk reject is powerful — avoid it unless every selected row shares the same problem.

action.title: 🚫 Reject control
action.description:
Reject opens a confirmation where you should explain why.

The tour does not confirm — write a reason the family can act on.

empty.title: 📭 Empty inbox
empty.description: No pending receipts means there is nothing to reject right now.

intro.title: 📋 Take attendance
intro.description:
Attendance belongs to a concrete section (class group), not the whole cohort.

You mark who was present for scheduled meeting days so reports and family views stay accurate.

root.title: 🏫 Attendance workspace
root.description:
This panel is scoped to the section you opened.

If you landed elsewhere, open Academic → cohort → section → Attendance first.

viewTabs.title: 👁️ View modes
viewTabs.description:
Switch between day and matrix views when both are available.

Matrix is useful for spotting patterns across several sessions.

matrix.title: ▦ Attendance grid
matrix.description:
Each cell is a student on a meeting date. Mark present, absent, or late per your institute rules.

Changes usually save as you go — check before leaving.

tip.title: 💡 Tip
tip.description:
Take attendance soon after class so memories stay fresh.

Families may see attendance signals in the parent portal calendar.

intro.title: ٪ Partial scholarship (guide only)
intro.description:
A percent scholarship reduces monthly tuition for one student without changing the section’s base price.

This tour shows the billing panel. Do not save until you intend to apply the discount.

panel.title: 🎓 Scholarship panel
panel.description:
Open the student’s Payments / billing tab to reach scholarships.

Institute-wide promotions are separate under Finance.

discountFields.title: ✏️ Percent fields
discountFields.description:
Enter a percent between 1 and 99 for a partial grant.

Document why in notes if your process requires an audit trail.

saveGuide.title: 💾 Save — after the tour
saveGuide.description:
Save applies the scholarship for real. Review the percent, then save yourself when ready.

The tour never submits.

intro.title: 🎁 Full scholarship (guide only)
intro.description:
A 100% scholarship covers monthly tuition for the student while they remain enrolled under this grant.

Treat full waivers carefully — confirm eligibility before saving.

panel.title: 🎓 Scholarship panel
panel.description:
Same billing panel as partial scholarships; choose the full-coverage option or 100%.

Enrollment fees may still apply depending on institute rules.

discountFields.title: ✏️ Full coverage
discountFields.description:
Set the discount to 100% (or the full-scholarship control your form exposes).

Double-check the student identity before applying.

saveGuide.title: 💾 Save — after the tour
saveGuide.description:
Saving activates the full scholarship. Finish review, then save yourself when ready.

Closing the tour does not apply changes.

intro.title: 💳 Mercado Pago (guide only)
intro.description:
Online card payments for Chile and Argentina are configured under Finance → Settings.

This tour never saves credentials — paste keys only when you are ready after the tour.

settingsRoot.title: ⚙️ Finance settings
settingsRoot.description: Gateway cards and billing currency live on this settings tab — not in the payment inbox.

card.title: 🇨🇱 Mercado Pago Chile
card.description:
Chile and Argentina each have their own Mercado Pago card. Start with the country that matches your institute.

Argentina’s card is similar further down the page.

credentials.title: 🔑 Access token & webhook
credentials.description:
Paste the Access Token and webhook secret from your Mercado Pago dashboard.

Never commit these to git or share them in chat.

saveGuide.title: 💾 Save — after the tour
saveGuide.description:
Save stores credentials for real. Finish the tour, verify the keys, then save yourself.

Closing the tour does not write secrets.

intro.title: 🏦 Flow Chile (guide only)
intro.description:
Flow is the Chile bank-transfer style gateway under Finance → Settings.

The tour explains fields only — it does not submit API keys.

settingsRoot.title: ⚙️ Finance settings
settingsRoot.description: Flow sits with other payment gateways on the Settings tab.

card.title: 🇨🇱 Flow Chile card
card.description: Enable or update Flow credentials in this card. Status shows whether keys are already stored.

credentials.title: 🔑 API key & secret
credentials.description:
Enter API key and secret from Flow’s merchant panel.

Leave blanks when you only want to rotate one value later.

saveGuide.title: 💾 Save — after the tour
saveGuide.description: Saving activates Flow for real. Confirm keys offline, then save yourself when ready.

intro.title: 💱 Billing currency (guide only)
intro.description:
Institute-wide currency labels fees, invoices, and gateways.

Changing it is rare — the tour never saves.

settingsRoot.title: ⚙️ Finance settings
settingsRoot.description: Currency lives at the top of Settings, above gateway cards.

currencySection.title: 💰 Currency block
currencySection.description: This section controls the default ISO currency for tuition and related fees.

currencyField.title: ✏️ Currency selector
currencyField.description: Pick a standard code (CLP, ARS, USD, …) or Other for a custom ISO-4217 value.

warning.title: ⚠️ Affects everyone
warning.description: A currency change applies institute-wide. Coordinate with finance before saving.

saveGuide.title: 💾 Save — after the tour
saveGuide.description: Save writes the new currency for real. Double-check the code, then save yourself when ready.

intro.title: 🎟️ Event payment approval (guide only)
intro.description:
Paid events list receipts on the event detail Payments tab.

This tour never clicks Approve on a real pending payment.

paymentsTab.title: 💳 Payments tab
paymentsTab.description: Switch to Payments to review registrations, receipts, and approval actions.

panel.title: 📋 Payments panel
panel.description: Summary counts, filters, and the list of payment rows appear here.

filters.title: 🔎 Status filters
filters.description: Filter pending, approved, or rejected rows before acting on a receipt.

approveGuide.title: ✅ Approve control
approveGuide.description: Pending rows show Approve after optional notes. Confirm yourself only when the receipt is valid.

empty.title: 📭 No rows yet
empty.description: When no payments match the filter, the list is empty — try All or Pending when registrations arrive.

intro.title: 🎓 Bulk section scholarships (guide only)
intro.description:
Section collections can apply the same discount percent to many students at once.

The tour opens the modal for orientation but never confirms bulk apply.

collectionsRoot.title: 📊 Section collections
collectionsRoot.description: Finance → Collections for a section: matrix, settings, history, scholarships, and enrollment tabs.

scholarshipsTab.title: 🏷️ Scholarships tab
scholarshipsTab.description: Optional tab listing active scholarships and another entry point for bulk assign.

bulkTrigger.title: ➕ Bulk scholarship
bulkTrigger.description: On the matrix tab toolbar, open bulk assign to set percent, months, and scope.

modalGuide.title: 📝 Bulk modal
modalGuide.description: Choose discount, period, and all/selected/pending students. Confirm only after the tour when data is correct.

intro.title: 🏛️ Initial setup currency (guide only)
intro.description:
Greenfield Initial setup sets institute currency on Legal & billing — separate from Finance settings edits.

The tour never finishes the wizard for you.

stepIndicator.title: 📍 Wizard progress
stepIndicator.description: Step indicator shows where you are in the eight-step Initial setup flow.

panel.title: 📋 Step panel
panel.description: Each step collects branding, contact, or operational defaults before go-live.

currencyField.title: 💱 Billing currency
currencyField.description: Pick ISO currency for tuition labels institute-wide. Other legal and billing fields live on this step too.

navGuide.title: ➡️ Continue wizard
navGuide.description: Use Back/Continue to move steps. Finish Initial setup yourself when every field is correct.

intro.title: 📰 New blog article (guide only)
intro.description:
CMS blog drafts live under Content → Blog. This tour opens the editor and explains fields.

It does not publish — keep status as draft until you are ready.

editor.title: 📝 Article editor
editor.description: Locales, title, body, materials, and publishing meta are edited here.

titleField.title: ✏️ Title
titleField.description: Write a clear public title for the active locale tab.

body.title: 📄 Body
body.description: Rich text for the article. Attach media carefully — uploads are real even before publish.

meta.title: 🏷️ Status & meta
meta.description: Draft vs published, tags, schedule, and pin. Prefer Draft while learning the editor.

saveGuide.title: 💾 Save — after the tour
saveGuide.description: Save persists the draft. Publishing is a separate status choice — finish fields, then save yourself.

intro.title: ✍️ Teacher blog draft (guide only)
intro.description:
Teachers use the same CMS editor but often set status to pending_review for staff approval.

The tour does not submit for review.

editor.title: 📝 Article editor
editor.description: Locales, title, body, materials, and publishing meta are edited here.

titleField.title: ✏️ Title
titleField.description: Write a clear public title for the active locale tab.

body.title: 📄 Body
body.description: Rich text for the article. Attach media carefully — uploads are real even before publish.

meta.title: 🏷️ Tags & schedule
meta.description: Tags, schedule, and pin options sit alongside status.

reviewStatus.title: 📮 Pending review
reviewStatus.description: Choose pending_review when a teacher draft needs admin approval before publish.

saveGuide.title: 💾 Save — after the tour
saveGuide.description: Save persists the draft. Move to pending_review and save yourself when the article is ready.

intro.title: 🔑 Reset password (guide only)
intro.description:
Admins can set a new portal password from a user’s Security tab.

This tour never applies a password — confirm yourself after the tour if needed.

securityTab.title: 🛡️ Security tab
securityTab.description: Open Security on the user dossier to reach password and document-reset tools.

securityPanel.title: 🔐 Security panel
securityPanel.description: Password tools appear here when you may edit the profile.

passwordSection.title: ✏️ Password controls
passwordSection.description: Choose manual entry or auto-generate, copy safely, then apply only when confirmed.

applyGuide.title: ✅ Apply — after the tour
applyGuide.description: Apply opens a confirmation. The tour stops here on purpose — never apply during a practice pass unless intentional.

intro.title: 📥 Import users (guide only)
intro.description:
Bulk onboarding uses a spreadsheet dry-run, then a confirmed apply.

This tour never starts an import job.

titleBlock.title: 👥 Import screen
titleBlock.description: Users → Import is for CSV/XLSX bulk create and optional updates.

chooseFile.title: 📂 Choose file
chooseFile.description: Select a spreadsheet to dry-run. Invalid rows are reported before anything is written.

tip.title: 💡 After the tour
tip.description: Review the preview modal carefully. Confirm apply only when counts look right — closing the tour does not import.

adminChangelogPage.title: What's new
adminChangelogPage.lead: History of features added to the product. This is not the audit log: it does not show who edited a student or a payment.

adminGlossaryPage.title: Terms glossary
adminGlossaryPage.lead: Quick reference for the vocabulary used across admin, finance, and academic screens. Expand any entry for a fuller explanation and related terms.

adminHelpGlossary.hierarchyLead: Most academic work follows this order. People and billing connect at the section level.
hierarchySteps: Cohort — one container per school year
Section — class group with schedule, teacher, and enrollments inside the cohort
Course — learning unit or material track inside a section

cohort.title: Cohort
cohort.body:
The top-level academic container for one school year (for example “Cohort 2026”). There is typically one cohort per calendar year — morning and afternoon schedules are not separate cohorts; they live in sections inside the same cohort.

You create the cohort first, then add sections and courses inside it. Archived cohorts stay available for history and reports.

current-cohort.title: Current cohort
current-cohort.body:
The cohort marked as the institute’s operating year right now. Public registration, assigning students to sections from user detail, and several finance views use this cohort as the default context.

Only one cohort should be current at a time. Mark it from Cohorts & sections when families should enroll into that year.

section.title: Section
section.body:
A concrete class inside a cohort: name, weekly schedule, assigned teacher, capacity, and enrolled students. Shifts (morning, afternoon, Saturday, etc.) are defined here — not by creating another cohort.

Attendance, grades, section messages, and monthly billing usually run at section level. A student can be enrolled in one or more sections depending on institute rules.

course.title: Course
course.aliases: Also: unit, learning content in a section
course.body:
The teaching unit or content track inside a section — materials, tasks, mini-tests, or ordered activities families and students see in the portal.

Courses are not the same as sections: the section is the live group; courses are what that group works through. They may follow a learning route or stay in free mode.

academic-hub.title: Cohorts & sections
academic-hub.body:
The admin home for cohorts and sections: create cohorts, open a cohort to manage its sections, copy section designs from a previous year, mark the current cohort, and jump to transfers or retention for that context.

If you are unsure where academic structure lives, start here.

learning-route.title: Learning route
learning-route.body:
A reusable ordered sequence of content from the repository. Sections can attach a route so students progress step by step, or remain in free mode without a fixed path.

Routes are defined globally under Contents; sections pick one when configuring the class.

student.title: Student
student.body:
The person who attends classes. Students have a portal login (email or institutional address for minors), profile data, section enrollments, grades, attendance, and billing rows.

Minors are usually linked to a guardian account for payments and messages.

guardian.title: Guardian / tutor
guardian.aliases: Also: parent, apoderado, family account (role Tutores)
guardian.body:
The adult responsible for a student in the portal — often a parent or legal guardian. In the database the role is parent/Tutores, but staff and families may say tutor or apoderado.

Guardians can pay fees, read messages, and manage linked children. Link them at registration, import, or from the student’s admin profile.

teacher.title: Teacher
teacher.body:
Staff who run sections: take attendance, publish grades, message their classes, and propose student transfers. Teachers see only their assigned sections in the teacher portal.

Assign the teacher when creating or editing a section.

enrollment-fee.title: Enrollment fee (matrícula)
enrollment-fee.body:
The one-time or annual charge to confirm a seat, separate from recurring monthly fees. Promotions and coupons may apply to enrollment only, monthly fees only, or both — check each code’s scope.

Recording enrollment as paid unlocks related billing rules in some flows.

section-enrollment.title: Section enrollment
section-enrollment.aliases: Also: active seat in a class
section-enrollment.body:
The link between a student and a section for the cohort cycle — who sits in which group, with start/end dates and status. Without enrollment, the student will not appear in that section’s attendance, grades, or billing.

Assign from Cohorts & sections queues, user detail, imports, or approved transfers.

promotion.title: Promotion
promotion.body:
An institute-defined discount code with rules: percent or fixed amount, enrollment vs monthly scope, optional month limits, stacking, expiry, and global use counts. Families or staff enter the code when paying.

Managed under Finance → Promotions. Retiring a promotion stops new uses but keeps history.

coupon.title: Coupon
coupon.body:
A simpler discount code with validity windows and usage limits, managed separately from promotions. Use coupons for short campaigns; use promotions when you need fine-grained rules (enrollment-only, stackable, monthly month caps).

Both reduce what families pay — they are different admin tools, not interchangeable labels.

transfer.title: Transfer
transfer.body:
Moving a student from one section to another (often within the same cohort). Teachers propose transfers from their portal; administrators approve and execute them from the transfer inbox or academic views.

Keeps enrollment history auditable instead of deleting and re-adding manually.

public-registration.title: Public registration
public-registration.body:
A family-submitted request from the public site before the account is fully provisioned. Admins review new registrations, create or link student and guardian accounts, and assign sections in the current cohort.

Toggle visibility of the public form in institute settings.

health.summaryScreenReader: Section summary: {students} active students, capacity utilization {capacity}, attendance rate {attendance}.
health.chartEmpty: Not enough data for this chart yet.
health.chartHelpAttendanceBody:
A single horizontal stacked bar shows how all attendance marks split across statuses (segment length is the raw count; the full bar is every mark in the section).

Counts come from the section_attendance table: for each active enrollment we count rows with each status (batched for performance).

The headline attendance rate in the summary strip uses (present + late + excused) divided by (present + absent + late + excused), rounded to a whole percent.
health.chartHelpTasksBody:
Radial bands show the same three counts as before: each arc is one progress bucket (not opened, opened, completed).

This classifies each student_task_progress row that joins active task instances for this section with your active enrollments.

Instances are non-archived task_instances for this section (capped on the server). Each progress status maps to Not opened, Opened, or Completed (including completed late).

If some enrollments do not yet have a row for every instance, row totals can be lower than instances times students.
health.chartHelpCapacityBody:
A treemap uses rectangle area proportional to each value: larger means more seats in that bucket.

It compares seats already filled by active students with seats still free up to the section effective capacity.

Filled seats equals the number of active enrollments. Free seats is effective capacity minus active students, never negative.

Capacity values come from the section configuration you maintain under Configuration.
health.chartHelpPaymentsBody:
A donut is the clearest part-to-whole view for exactly two buckets: active students with billing follow-up versus those clear.

It splits active students between those flagged for billing follow-up and those considered clear.

The split uses the same per-student debt signal computed when this page loads (aligned with the Fees matrix): students marked with debt count toward follow-up needed.
health.chartHelpEngagementBody:
Three separate columns compare unrelated magnitudes (different units); column height is the raw count—do not add them as if they were one total.

Engagement points sums profiles.engagement_points for every active student in this section.

Material opens counts portal user_events in roughly the last 30 days (UTC) for those students whose event entity starts with the material prefix.

Learning area events counts user_events for the learning-route entity in the same rolling window. See the note above the charts about the 30-day window.
health.chartHelpAssessmentsBody:
Two horizontal bars share one numeric axis so you can compare published grade rows with pending slots at a glance.

Published grades counts enrollment_assessment_grades rows with status published for active enrollments in this section.

Pending slots is max(expected minus published, 0), where expected is cohort assessment definitions for the parent cohort times active students when both are positive.

Cohort assessment definitions are counted from the cohort assessments catalog.
health.chartHelpReadinessBody:
Two simple columns show how many route steps sit in each readiness flag (needs support versus teacher override).

Each column counts readiness rows on the learning route assigned to this section, computed when the route workspace loads.

These are instructional flags on the route, not attendance.

In free flow or when no route is assigned, counts are usually zero.

faqs.q: Is CentroListo Presence really free?
faqs.a: Yes. You can create the institution page for free with a ready-made template. An administrator reviews the account before it goes live. You can open up to three sites. Students and tuition are not included.

faqs.q: Can I customize the page?
faqs.a: You can edit the content and identity options in the template. An exclusive design is quoted separately.

faqs.q: Do I need Management to have a website?
faqs.a: No. You can use Presence on its own.

faqs.q: What if the institution grows?
faqs.a: You can look at Management and Ecosystem to add administration and a family space. The change is not automatic.

faqs.q: Does a custom design have a fixed price?
faqs.a: No. The quote follows the scope of the project.

faqs.q: Are payment gateway fees included?
faqs.a: No. Each gateway states its fees separately.

faqs.q: How long does it take to launch my center on CentroListo.cl?
faqs.a: Technical infrastructure and your domain go live in under 24 hours. With your logos, schedules, and payment credentials, full onboarding takes 3 to 5 business days.

faqs.q: Do students and parents see the CentroListo brand or my academy's brand?
faqs.a: They see 100% your institution's brand: your custom domain, your logo, your colors, your email sender, and your academy icon when they install the PWA.

faqs.q: What if I already have active students mid-year?
faqs.a: Our background CSV importer and enrollment tools let you migrate cohorts, sections, students, and guardians without interrupting classes.

faqs.q: Why does an isolated database matter for my center?
faqs.a: Your student roster, minor records, and financial data are never mixed in shared tables with other companies. You get independent backups and strong technical alignment with Chile Law 21.719.
